3(a).stem_md:
A producer sells a product in two distinct markets: Market X and Market Y. The demand functions in each market are given by:
Market X : $Q_1 = 21 - 0.1P_1$
Market Y : $Q_2 = 50 - 0.4P_2$
The total cost of production is given by $\text{TC} = 2000 + 10Q$ where $Q = Q_1 + Q_2$.
The producer must charge the same price in both markets.

**Required :**
**Analyze** the price that the producer will charge in order to maximize profits and also **Assess** the maximum profit.
3(a).answer_md:
Calculation of profit maximization price and associated profit
When the producer does not discriminate between market X & market Y and charges the same price, the two demand functions can be aggregated and $P_1$ and $P_2$ may be replaced by a uniform price, say $P$.

Thus, we have $Q = Q_1 + Q_2 = (21 - 0.1P) + (50 - 0.4P) = 71 - 0.5P$
Or, $P = 142 - 2Q$
The total revenue is given by
$\text{TR} = P \times Q = (142 - 2Q) \times Q = 142Q - 2Q^2$
$\text{MR} = d/dQ\,(142Q - 2Q^2) = 142 - 4Q$

$\text{Marginal Cost} = d/dQ\,(2000 + 10Q) = 10$
For maximization of profit, $\text{MR} = \text{MC}$
$142 - 4Q = 10$
$Q = 33$

Putting $Q = 33$ in the equation $P = 142 - 2Q$, we get $P = 76$
Therefore, the profit maximizing price is 76.

Assessment of Maximum Profit (Rs)
$\text{Profit} = \text{TR} - \text{TC} = P \times Q - (2000 + 10Q)$
$= 33 \times 76 - (2000 + 10 \times 33) = 178$
The associated profit is 178

Computation of Present Value (PV) of Cash Flows

YEAR | Cashflows (₹ in Lakh) | Discount Rate PVIF (15%) | Present Value ₹ in Lakh
---|---|---|---
1 | (10) (Negative) | 0.8696 | (8.696)
2 | 5 | 0.7562 | 3.781
3 | 10 | 0.6576 | 6.576
4 | 15 | 0.5718 | 8.577
5 | 20 | 0.4972 | 9.944
TOTAL | | | 20.182

Assessment of Value of Firm:
(i) Total sum of present value = ₹ 20.18
(ii) $\text{Terminal Value}_t = (\text{Cash Flow}_{t+1} / r - g_{\text{stable}})$
$\text{Cash Flow}_{t+1} = \text{Cash Flow}_t(1 + g)$
$= \text{₹ }20(1 + 0.05) = 21$ Lakhs.
$\text{Terminal Value} = 21 / (0.08 - 0.05)$
$= \text{₹ }700$ Lakhs.
$\text{Present Value of Terminal Value} = \text{₹ }700 \times (0.4972) = \text{₹ }348.04$ Lakh
$\text{Value of the Firm} = \text{₹ }(20.18 + 348.04) = \text{₹ }368.22$ Lakh

7(a).answer_md:
(i) Calculation of Swap Ratio:

Particulars | RAJ Ltd. | PREET Ltd.
---|---|---
EAT (₹) | 2000 lakh | 400 lakh
No of shares outstanding | 200 lakh | 100 lakh
P/E Ratio | 10 | 5
EPS (₹) | $2000/200 = 10$ | $400/100 = 4$
Market Price /Share $(\text{EPS} \times \text{P/E})$ (₹) | 100 | 20

Therefore, swap ratio in terms of market prices $= \text{MPS of target firm} / \text{MPS of acquiring firm} = 20/100 = 0.20$ i.e. 1 share of RAJ Ltd for 5 Shares of Preet Ltd.

(ii) Calculation of Market Price after acquisition:
EPS of Raj Ltd. after acquisition $= (2000 + 400) / (200 + 0.2 \times 100)$
$= 2400 / 220 = \text{₹ }10.91$

Therefore, expected market price per share of RAJ Ltd. with the same P/E Ratio of 10 will be $= \text{EPS} \times \text{P/E} = \text{₹ }10.91 \times 10 = \text{₹ }109.10$

7(b).answer_md:
(i) Calculation of post-acquisition benefit:
Rate of Return required by the investors of BODON Ltd. is given by
$K_e = (D_1 / P) + g = 1/15 + 0.07 = 0.1367$ or 13.67%
If $g = 8\%$, market price per share of BODON Ltd. $= 1 \times 1.08 / (0.1367 - 0.08)$
$= \text{₹ }19.05$
$\text{Benefits of acquisition} = \text{PV of BODON Ltd. with merger} - \text{PV of BODON Ltd. without merger}$
$= (19.05 - 15) \times 20{,}00{,}000 = \text{₹ }81{,}00{,}000$

(ii) Cost of acquisition to DODON Ltd.:
1. If it pays cash compensation of ₹ 17 per share:
$\text{Cost of acquisition} = \text{Cash Compensation} - \text{PV of BODON Ltd.}$
$= (17 \times 20{,}00{,}000) - (15 \times 20{,}00{,}000)$
$= \text{₹ }40$ lakh

2. If offers one share for every three shares:
In this case share of BODON Ltd. in the combined entity will be
$= (1/3 \times 20{,}00{,}000) / (60{,}00{,}000 + 1/3 \times 20{,}00{,}000) = 0.10$
$\text{Value of the merged entity} = \text{Value of DODON Ltd.} + \text{Value of BODON Ltd} + \text{Synergy}$
$= (60\text{ lakh} \times \text{₹ }48) + (20\text{ lakh} \times \text{₹ }15) + 81\text{ lakh}$
$= \text{₹ }3{,}261\text{ lakh}$
Cost of acquisition to DODON Ltd. given the exchange ratio,
$= \text{The value of what BODON's shareholder's get} - \text{the value what they give up}$
$= 0.10 \times 3{,}261 - 300 = \text{₹ }26.10\text{ lakh}$
